name: Maroon and red stripes (1985)
description: People Express's scheme as worn in the mid-1980s: an almond (warm off-white) body, fin and belly. Along the body, nose to tail, a broad maroon band over the cabin windows, then a thin almond line, a red band through the windows, and under it two red-orange stripes, the lower one thinner, each set off by a thin almond line. All the edges are level, so the bands run off the nose under and around the windshield and off the tail cone. 'PEOPLExpress' in almond on the maroon band behind the forward door, slanted on the 727s and 737s and upright on the 747s. On the almond fin the faces mark in maroon: two parallel lines running down the fin, each a person's profile facing forward in its lower half. Polished engines on the 737s and 747s, almond side nacelles on the 727s, gray wings.

sources.title: N574PE B727-243 PEOPLExpress ORD 24DEC86 (CC BY-SA 3.0, Ken Fielding)
sources.note: 727-200 N574PE at Chicago O'Hare, left side from a little above, 24 December 1986 (through a terminal window): every band's height (against the crown and belly at 11-12 m back), the title's place, size and slant, the fin's mark, the almond nacelles. Taken at an angle, so lengths are read near each feature, not from the nose.

sources.title: People Express Boeing 737-217 N431PE at Newark, December 1983 (CC BY-SA 2.0, Aero Icarus)
sources.note: 737-200 N431PE, left side, side-on with a long lens: the bands' heights against the cabin windows, crown and belly aft of the wing, the title's place, size and slant, the fin's mark.

sources.title: N417PE Boston, 10 August 1984 (CC BY 2.0, Pete Macklin)
sources.note: 737-100 N417PE, right side, side-on in sun: the bands against the windows (they agree with N431PE's within 3-5 cm), the colors, the fin's mark facing forward on this side too, a slanted title.

sources.title: N407PE Newark, 29 September 1984 (CC BY-SA 2.0, Pete Macklin)
sources.note: 737-100 N407PE from ahead on the left: the title close up (too oblique to read its slant), the bands running off the nose under the windshield, the polished engines. Evidence of the look; not measured (oblique).

sources.title: N417PE, Boeing 737-100 of People Express Airlines at Logan International Airport, 1984 (CC BY-SA 2.0, Pete Macklin)
sources.note: Another view of N417PE, right side: a check of the tail cone and the fin.

sources.title: Boeing 747-143, PEOPLExpress (GFDL 1.2, Tim Rees)
sources.note: 747-100, left side, 1986, 1024 px: the bands against the main deck's windows and the doors, the title, the fin's mark, polished engines. Low resolution: the thin lines are read to about a pixel (5 cm).

sources.title: Boeing 747-227B, PEOPLExpress (GFDL 1.2, Tim Rees)
sources.note: 747-200 N602PE, right side, 1983: the title reads forward from the right too, the fin's mark faces forward.

sources.title: People Express Boeing 747 at London Gatwick in June 1983 (CC BY-SA 3.0, Eduard Marmet)
sources.note: 747, right side, June 1983: the fin's mark and the bands to the tail cone.

sources.title: Boeing 747-227B, PeoplExpress (GFDL 1.2, Jon Proctor)
sources.note: 747-200 N602PE climbing, 1984: the almond belly and gray wings from below.

sources.title: People Express Airlines (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Dates: first flights April 1981 from Newark; merged into Continental Airlines on 1 February 1987. The fleet: 737-100/200s, 727-200s and 747-100/200s. Evidence only.

titles.style: 'PEOPLExpress' in almond, slanted about 14°: heavy squarish sans-serif, 'PEOPLE' in capitals run tight together with 'xpress' in lowercase (the p's tail below the line), on the maroon band behind the forward door.

logos.description: The 'faces' mark in maroon: two parallel lines running down the fin side by side, each a straight stroke from near the fin's top, sloping down and forward like the back of a head, that becomes a person's profile in its lower half (brow, nose, lips and chin) facing forward. Two people side by side, drawn as simple even lines. Facing forward on both sides.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 for ghost flights on 727-200 N574PE (December 1986), with the 737 (on the 737-300 shape, for the 737-100/200) and the 747 (on the 747-400 passenger shape, for the 747-100/200) as types. Every paint edge is one height in meters along the body, from the nose to the tail, with a point at each of the shape's crown and belly points (and between them to hold within 0.3 mm), so the bands draw level and run off the nose and tail cone where the outline crosses them. The 727's bands (above its centerline: maroon 0.78-1.63 m, red 0.25-0.72 m, stripes -0.09-0.15 m and -0.30 to -0.15 m) were read against the crown and belly; the 737's and 747's against their cabin windows, so the windows sit in the red band as on the aircraft. The 727 photo was taken at an angle from above through glass: its heights are good to about 5 cm, its lengths less so. The shapes are stand-ins: the 727-200 shape is the freighter (no cabin windows drawn), the 737-300 is longer than a -100/-200 and the 747-400 has the longer hump. The title's slant was measured from the lean of the letters' stems against the doors' edges in the same unflipped photo (the camera's angle leans both alike): about 14° on the 727 (N574PE: the stems lean 5° forward, the door's edges 8-10° back), about 22° on the 737s (N431PE 23°, N417PE 22°) and upright on the 747 (within about 4°: a 1024 px photo). N407PE's is too oblique to read. Each is drawn with its own wordmark mark. Whether the two lower stripes are a different red from the window band is uncertain: in sun on the 737s and 747s they read more orange, on the 727 in dull light the same. Some aircraft had a white radome (N417PE); most photos show it almond. The registration (black, on the aft body) isn't drawn. No US flag is seen in the photos. The fin's mark shows two people's profiles: a drawing of it should keep to simple, even lines. Refitted 2026-11-24 on the passenger 727 (shapes/B722-passenger.json): on N574PE the red band runs 0.25 m over and under the windows' middle (it sat low, the windows across its top), the almond line over it 0.09 m, the red-orange stripes 0.33-0.57 and 0.63-0.77 m under the windows' middle; level on the cabin.

B733.note: The 737s' bands sit a little lower and narrower against the crown than the 727's (maroon 0.71-1.33 m, red 0.20-0.66 m, stripes -0.07-0.14 m and -0.23 to -0.13 m above the shape's centerline), measured against the windows on N431PE and N417PE. Polished engines. The fin's mark nearly fills the fin's height, aft of its middle.

B742.note: On the 747s the bands are bigger (maroon 0.91-2.03 m, red -0.42-0.74 m, stripes -0.82 to -0.52 m and -1.08 to -0.92 m above the shape's centerline), read against the main deck's windows on a 1024 px photo taken from ahead (heights scaled by the doors' height, lengths by the spacing of the first two doors); the lowest stripe is barely resolved. The hump over them is almond. The title runs from the first door nearly to the second. Polished engines. The fin's mark is narrower on the 747's tall fin than drawn here: the mark keeps the 737's proportions. On the 747-100/-200 shape (shapes/B742.json) since 2026-11-25: the title is clear under the upper deck's three windows, which sit on the almond above the maroon as on the 747-143 (1986).
